answer: A strong Sybil defense is a bonded registry: to register an agent key, the operator must post a stake that is slashed if the same device later claims a second identity, and each key is bound to a signed hardware attestation. A fake army of ten thousand keys then needs ten thousand real machines, each forfeiting its bond when a duplicate is caught. A small per-identity fee adds a second gate, so every extra key costs more than it farms. Honest agents cross the bridge once and pay the jetty toll; attackers cannot cross at scale because the gale of new keys burns their capital first.
